items.note: Story 1: Association, 1889, Larrow Green, Gideon Vose president to 1911, creamery 1891.
Article VII: paid by butterfat by test not weight; station test governs.
'Under payment by weight, nothing that followed would have cost anyone a dollar.'
Loomis secretary 1901, Teague bookkeeper 1905, Sill buttermaker.
Selby Vose, son (not nephew), manager from 1913.
Story 6: station-gain line entered every year, 1898 entry, 5 1/4 percent, carried to general account.
Ostrey Hollow station, 7 miles, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed of Larrow Green.
Weighed in, composite samples, 17.6 c.c. charge, fat column read in bottle; cream to Larrow Green, skim back.
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Invoice itemised: six dozen 17.6 c.c. pipettes, 12 dozen bottles, acid measure, tester, freight, $77.93.
Story 3 and 4: 0.19 'flat as a floor', same in July and February, in every month.
The point that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette (none in the county) appears only in Section F, not in Section A.
Keddie 1861-1934, 29 seasons 1896-1924, dismissed 30 April 1925.
Test book, five columns, errors struck through and initialed.
1896 average 3.80 on borrowed glass; 3.61 from 1898 within 0.03.
8 May to 10 July 1911, borrowed measure, 3.80, fell back same day, '?' in book.
Orra Brant, Emmet's sister; tester was brother-in-law of the patron who lost most.
1919 circular present, but Keddie's statement that he cannot say why the figures are what they are is only in Section F; Section A quotes only his denial of taking cream.
Died February 1934 with imputation on him; test book to Historical Rooms 1959.
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Emmet Brant's the largest.
Weigh book from 1 January 1897; scales agreed.
Complaints from 1902; keeps 0.17 (vs Larrow Green 3.78) separate from 0.19 (vs truth).
Grigg committee sampled Jan-Mar 1908, blamed wet hay; reported as finding and refuted.
200,000 lb at 3.42; proportional loss, 4.56 recorded was 0.24 short.
Roy kept it after 1929, lent it to Ivy 1958, to Hazel at Roy's death 1962.
Jerome Cudd, Alder Corners, Vessey County, Redlow Ridge; 1913/1914 reconciled, opening given as 1914.
From 1915 four of six Bottom men hauled summer flush over the ridge.
Own new glassware, never compared figures, another county; 'independent instrument'.
Same cows read 3.80 at Alder Corners vs 3.61 at station, gap 0.19; sixteen seasons 1915-1930 given (though run then narrows the short-glass overlap to eight seasons, which is unbolded context).
Same cows' milk on an independent instrument kills hay (summer gap) and watering (Cudd's curd).
Rosalie, daughter not niece, took over 1941, copied figures for Ivy 1958.
Strawn, Ordell circuit 1907-1936, related to nobody.
Story 7: never found added water with his lactometer.
12 June 1923, burette, condemned the whole crate.
Quotes 'I did not weigh what it has cost them'.
Order 28 June, ack 2 July, in use July 1923; 1924 average 3.80; 'Nobody connected the two facts.'
Crate to loft; 1923 notebook in Farland library since 1947.
Petition January 1925.
Frick board, 17 March-4 May 1925, three sittings, two in weigh room.
Water (Vose), theft (Teague), hay (1908 report); none accepted.
Four books listed incl. Strawn's 1923 notebook, but Section A never states that notebook held the answer and was read for its other lines; that point is only in Section F.
Dismissed 30 April 1925; 'finds no cause established'; $3,800 without admission, charged to station account.
One fifth of $19,000 stated, but not that the award was charged to the very account where the loss accumulated as 'gain'.
Ivy, Ansel's granddaughter, b. 1931, graduate student at Farland; Vaught co-author.
Section A shows her getting individual records but never states she assembled records that had never been in the same room; that framing is only in G.
February 1958, loft, nine survived.
95% of truth, 3.80 reads 3.61, 0.19; richer milk loses more; 1 May 1897-12 June 1923.
40,000,000 lb, 76,000 lb, $19,000 at 25c; Story 6 ties 76,000 to the ledger's gain.
Bulletin 471 October 1958; 35, 33, 24 years.
Granddaughter.
Ansel > Duncan > Ivy.
Second cousins derived via Roy and Duncan as first cousins.
'I accept full siblings' (and E row 5 'Full, by majority'); also says half siblings would change the answer to 'half second cousins', contrary to key.
Gideon Vose.
Gideon wrote Article VII; son enforced father's rule, blamed patrons not instrument.
Headline: 'No relationship ... is established, and the best evidence says there was none'; E row 4 resolves it on Duncan's denial. Never declares it unsettleable.
Two narrators assert from talk, Duncan denies, no document records any link.
0.95, 95% of true.
76,000 = 5.26% of credited, 5.00% of received; denominators named.
$77.93 by line-item sum.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. short each.
26 years 42 days vs 25 full years 1898-1922; partial years reason given.
Abstains: cannot be determined; two memories, no document.
Variable: only the pipette.
Same tester, scales, bottles, acid, tester, patrons, herds, feed.
3.80 for nine weeks, back to 3.61 on 10 July.
Fault in station apparatus, rules out water/theft/feed; limits: size in c.c., which glass, lender unknown.
Ledger gain (Sill/Teague), 1911 test book, 1924 Strawn, Alder Corners (Cudd).
Independence argued; ledger gain and 1911 hold without 1958.
A09: 'Did the bookkeeper ever question the entries? No.' Definite assertion.
Yes, he knew the tests ran low; 1902 complaints, 1919 circular.
Manager from 1913, signed sheets with the gain line, 1919 circular, argued water at hearing.
A03: 'What Vose did not grasp is that the tests were false'; 'his conduct argues against it'. Asserts he did not know; abstains only on negligence vs wilful blindness.
E.g. farms six (majority), crate in loft, circular nine, Orra 1866, weigh book 1897, Selby 1913, 1924 average 3.80, with methods.
NT-1 16.27 (Vaught/Chronicle), NT-11 12 July (28 June order), NT-14 $77.39 (line sum), NT-20 and more, pairs named with breakers.
A04 (works books burned 1931), A06 (borrowed measure unsettled), A10 (by-law year) declined, with what is established.
Self-refutations: r15, r18, r20, r11, r05, r03.
16.72 vs 17.6, 95% of truth, proportional, onset 1 May 1897/1896 3.80, end 12 June 1923/1924 3.80.
Water (Vose, Sill) defeated by Strawn lactometer, Brant scales, Cudd.
Theft (Teague) defeated: cream arrived heavy; 1911; 1924.
Hay (Grigg, Kepp) defeated by Bulletin 214 0.05 winter/nothing summer vs flat 0.19.
A07: 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glassware? No.' ... 'It never looked at the glass.'
A05: 'The sources do not settle it'; lean given but final verdict cannot be determined.
About 142 words.
Invoice, test book, weigh book, Alder Corners book, ledger, inspector's notebook, arbitration.
Decoys attributed, not adopted; no wrong headline figures.
